### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **75** documentable anchor(s).

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 50 pages)`
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **50** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1b1fbd9a36f910cb622ce1d99b37fccc0fdd5795` — the merge of head `608a01fb65a47542a4570e3f733b1349c6f50391` into base `811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1b1fbd9a36f910cb622ce1d99b37fccc0fdd5795 && git checkout 1b1fbd9a36f910cb622ce1d99b37fccc0fdd5795
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec 608a01fb65a47542a4570e3f733b1349c6f50391 && git checkout -B drift-repro 811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec && git merge --no-ff 608a01fb65a47542a4570e3f733b1349c6f50391

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 811858c6595421c8b7ca1d05f546b0e11e947eec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5b98dea6f390568b34ae979ad61338f5d8365c0e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/sso-discovery-connect-time.md (declaration lines), packages/core/src/egress/guarded-fetch.ts, packages/core/src/egress/guarded-fetch.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-egress.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-egress.testkit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-connect-time.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-request-routing.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts + read, not reviewed: @better-auth/sso 1.7.12 dist/index.mjs, better-call 1.4.4 dist/router.mjs, @better-auth/core 1.7.12 adapter factory, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/transport.ts
Security-touching: yes

Inputs: the PR body and file list, the net diff against merge base `ca4ec2a2f1b`, the check-runs on this head, the dev evidence quoted in the brief. No card (a security-seat no-card order). Nothing was built or run; the vendor packages were read from their published tarballs at the locked versions. content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx is prose and is the seat's at ACCEPT.

The rule under review: every read plugin-auth has the server make of an identity provider connects only to an address judged public at connect time, by the one judgment (`classifyAddress`) the early register check also uses; a configured trusted origin is the one way out; reads at other origins and outside the request scope are untouched.

### ① Derived judgments

- Register discovery read (`/sso/register`, and the bridge, which re-dispatches by URL through `handleVendorRequest`): in scope, origin named from the body, sent through the guard. Right.
- Early register check (`refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic`): now `guard.judgeUrl`, the same resolver and policy as the connection, an address literal included. One judgment. Right. It newly refuses a literal the vendor predicate admits (`168.63.129.16`); the changeset says so. Right.
- Sign-out switch read on register and update-provider: its own scope with `targets: 'every'` around `judgeSignOutOfIdpCapability`, which makes the discovery read and nothing else (the stored row is read before the scope opens). Right.
- Callback token, key-set and userinfo reads: the vendor reads the stored `tokenEndpoint` / `jwksEndpoint` / `userInfoEndpoint`; `oidcConfigReadUrls` names exactly those members plus the issuer and discovery URL. The key-set read is a bare `fetch` resolved at call time, so the wrapper sees it. Right.
- Runtime discovery on sign-in and callback: the vendor admits that discovery URL and every endpoint the document names only on a configured trusted origin (`validateDiscoveryUrl`, `normalizeAndValidateUrl`), so those reads fall under the rule's one way out. Right.
- The configured-trust predicate the scope keeps is bound to the hook's own `ctx.context`; the body-named origins join a merged copy the vendor endpoint receives, never that object. A body-named origin does not exempt a read. Right.
- Provider lookup when the request names no provider reads the whole table: the adapter's unbounded `ssoProvider` read is count-then-read (`readEverySsoProviderRowWhenUnbounded`), so no provider is left unnamed past row 100. plugin-auth sets neither `defaultSSO` nor `redirectURI`. Right.
- Route match: `isSsoDiscoveryEgressPath` reads the path `betterAuthEndpointPath` answers (trailing slashes stripped); the vendor router answers 404 on a trailing-slash or doubled-slash spelling, so no spelling reaches the three endpoints outside the scope. Right.
- Redirects: the vendor reads with `redirect: 'manual'`, which the guarded fetch now hands to undici; a followed redirect would be judged hop by hop. Right.
- Refusal shape: the vendor's own `DiscoveryError` class (one ESM instance), `discovery_private_host` or `discovery_unexpected_error`; the text names the host and the origin, never the address. Register answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on the naming member from both the before-hook and the after-hook. Right.
- "Every other request (a database driver over HTTP, a host's own call) passes through untouched" (module docblock, PR body): wrong before the request's origins are named. See M1.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch, `@objectstack/core` patch. The diff publishes: one optional `AuthManagerOptions` member, one optional `EgressFetchInit` member, and narrowed runtime answers of the SSO doors. `Metadata-protocol: none`, so the repo rule (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3) ships it `patch` with its BREAKING banner; the banner, the ADR-0087 marker and both declaration lines are present in the changeset and the PR body. The removed `SsoHostResolver` type and the `resolve` input are not exported from the package index. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right declaration. Level: right. The BREAKING paragraph is incomplete: it names only an identity provider on a non-public address, and M1 moves a second population.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's four acceptance notes are answered in ① (runtime discovery; early check open on a lookup error; the guard's own transport; the wrapper's install).
- SQL push-down: S1.
- Gates: at this read `Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success; `Test Core` 1–10, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` were still in progress with no conclusion. No gate has concluded failure. The verdict below does not rest on the open ones.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R5 — graded in the seat's private notes. R5 is finding M1 below; R1–R4 do not block this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — `sso-discovery-egress.ts`, `runInSsoDiscoveryEgressScope` + `judges` + `declareSsoDiscoveryReadsOf`: the rule says reads at other origins are untouched, and inside the scope they are not until the origins are named. A vendor-endpoint scope starts `targets: 'every'` with no trust predicate, so every http(s) request made through the global fetch in that request is sent through the guard's public-only policy, whatever its origin. That window covers the vendor router's pre-hook work (rate-limit storage, plugin `onRequest`) and, on `/sign-in/sso` and `/sso/callback/*`, the hook's own `adapter.findMany` of `ssoProvider`, which runs before `declareSsoDiscoveryReads`. Two in-tree callers read the global fetch at call time: `driver-turso` `fetchBoundedBy` (`turso-driver.ts:1237`, every remote request when `timeout` is set) and `driver-odata` (`transport.ts:124`). For a datastore reached that way on an address that is not public (a self-hosted libSQL server on the deployment's network), the provider read is refused with a `DiscoveryError`, the `catch` then declares `'every'`, and every later datastore read of that sign-in or callback is refused too: SSO sign-in stops for that deployment, and its datastore is not an identity provider. On a public address the datastore's requests are re-sent over the guard's transport with the body re-read as text. A request that matches the three paths but never reaches the hook keeps the judge-everything scope for whatever it started. The test `until the request names its origins, every read is judged` pins a `db.internal.example` read going through the guard, so this is the design, not a slip; the docblock, the PR body and the changeset's BREAKING paragraph state the opposite. Owed: no read at an origin the request's provider configuration does not name is judged (the hook's own provider read included), a case that drives a real request with a non-provider read made through the global fetch before and after the hook and shows it sent as it was, or the changeset names the second population as a break.

S1 (should-fix) — `declareSsoDiscoveryReadsOf`: when the request names no `providerId` (the ordinary `/sign-in/sso` by email, domain or organization) or names one with no row (`/sso/callback/` with an unknown id, an unauthenticated door), the hook reads every `ssoProvider` row (a count, then the whole table) and parses each `oidcConfig` in the application, on every such request. `/sign-in/sso` makes no read the rule covers outside a configured trusted origin, so the materialisation serves nothing there; where it is needed the lookup pushes down (`domain`, `organizationId`, or the one row the vendor resolves). No reason is given in the diff (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5).

S2 (should-fix) — `installFetchWrapper`: the install is idempotent against a module-local variable (`installedFetch`), not against the global. Two copies of the module in one process (the dual build, a module-registry reset) each see the other's wrapper as a foreign fetch and wrap it again, alternately, one layer per request with no bound. A mark on the wrapper itself that every copy can read closes it.

N1 (nit) — `judgeSsoDiscoveryUrl` attaches a new `catch` to `defaultGuard` on every call, and its default guard has no logger.

N2 (nit) — the wrapper is never removed and replaces the global fetch's identity for the life of the process; a runtime that reads own properties of `fetch` loses them. Inert outside a scope, as stated.

Tried and held, and so not findings: isolation between concurrent requests (the scope is the AsyncLocalStorage store of one request; the wrapper holds no request state); the guard's own send leaving the scope (`scopeStore.exit`), so a stand-in that hands on to the global fetch is not judged twice; nested scopes on register (the sign-out read records its refusal on its own scope and answers it there); `getOrCreateAuth` running before the scope opens; an unresolved name (allowed at the early check, refused at the connection, nothing sent); the guard refusing every send where it cannot prove its connector is consulted.

**VERDICT: FAIL**

### ① Derived judgments

- A scope names no origin when it opens, and only a read at a named origin is judged (`judges`). So a read at any other origin, before or after naming, is sent as it was. Right, and it is now what the docblock, the PR body and the changeset say.
- A registration's origins: named from the body by the before-hook, which reads nothing now, ahead of the vendor endpoint. The vendor's register makes one read, the discovery document, at an origin in that set. Right.
- A stored provider's origins: named as its row is answered. The vendor reads its provider for sign-in and callback through `ctx.context.adapter.findOne` / `findMany` on model `ssoProvider` and through nothing else (`resolveOIDCProvider`, the `/sign-in/sso` lookups by provider, organization and domain; the callback's state carries an id, never a URL). The observed view names the row's issuer, discovery URL and four endpoints after the read resolves and before it returns the row, so no read of that provider can precede its naming. Right.
- The view is the adapter the endpoints hold: plugin `init` results are assigned onto the auth context in plugin order (`runPluginInit`), the agent-forward view is mounted earlier and is itself a delegating Proxy, so the context adapter is observer over agent view over the factory adapter. In either order the provider read passes through the observer. Right.
- The callback's second provider read runs on the transaction adapter (`getCurrentAdapter`), which the view does not cover. It is made after the token, key-set and userinfo reads, its row is only compared against the accepted reference, and nothing is read from it. Right.
- Runtime discovery on sign-in and callback still admits its URL and every endpoint the document names only on a configured trusted origin, the rule's one way out. Right.
- The sign-out read: its scope names the body's and the stored configuration's URLs, which cover the three places `judgeSignOutOfIdpCapability` takes its discovery URL from (body, stored, the issuer's well-known URL). Right.
- `runSsoDiscoveryEgress` refuses the request when the auth context's adapter does not carry the observed mark. Right as far as it goes: it proves the view is mounted, not that the vendor reads through it; what proves that is the callback cases on the real stack. See S3.
- The configured-trust predicate is still bound to the hook's own context; a body-named origin does not exempt a read. Right.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: both packages `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset and the PR body. The fix adds no published surface (`sso-discovery-egress.ts` is not exported from the package index; the new plugin is mounted internally). The changeset now states that only reads at the origins the provider's configuration names are judged, which is what the tree does; the BREAKING paragraph is complete.

### ③ Boundary flags

- SQL push-down: the hook's provider read is gone; the diff adds no read, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The observer reads the rows the vendor already asked for.
- Gates on this head at this read: 61 check-runs concluded success, 12 skipped, none failed. One `Check Changeset` run started 09:23Z was still in progress; an earlier run of the same check on this head concluded success. The seat reads its conclusion before it acts.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R6 — graded in the seat's private notes; none blocks this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

M1: closed. The scope starts empty and judges by origin alone; the before-hook reads nothing; the two real-stack CONTROL cases send datastore and counter-store reads on internal addresses through the global fetch before and after the provider read and show them sent as they were, while the token read in the same request is refused.

S1: closed. `declareSsoDiscoveryReadsOf` no longer reads the provider table.

S2: closed. The scope store and the wrapper mark are process-wide (`Symbol.for`); a second module copy finds both and does not wrap again, and a case pins it.

N1: closed for the repeated `catch`; the default guard outside a scope still has no logger (nit, unchanged).

N2: closed. The wrapper carries the wrapped fetch's own properties.

S3 (should-fix) — `AuthManager.runSsoDiscoveryEgress`: the refusal of a context whose adapter is not observed has no case. Removing the check, or the plugin's mount, leaves a suite that fails only through the callback cases, and nothing pins that the request is refused rather than sent on unjudged. One case that builds a manager whose context adapter lacks the mark and shows the three paths refused would pin it.

N3 (nit) — `isSsoProviderModel` and `oidcConfigReadUrls` hold the vendor's model name and member names as literals beside the comment naming `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12; the dependency is pinned exactly, and the real-stack callback cases go red if a later version stops reading through this view. A line in the upgrade notes for that dependency would say so where the next upgrader looks.

Tried and held: a provider read that bypasses the view (none in the vendor's sign-in or callback); a read racing its row's naming (the naming is awaited inside the read); a foreign fetch wrapper installed after this one (wrapped once more, the older layer sees an unjudged read and hands it on); concurrent requests (one store per request, no shared request state); nested scopes on register; the merge's added before-hook branches (all after the declaration).

The merge base is unchanged (`92ab0564ede`); no file outside those three moved. No card (a security-seat no-card order). Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- `runSsoDiscoveryEgress`, a context whose adapter does not carry the observed mark: was a thrown bare `Error`, is now a returned `503` with the envelope `success: false`, `error.code: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and one error line to the server log. Right: the return precedes `run`, so the vendor handler, its rate limiter, its hooks and its endpoint never start; nothing is read, judged or connected. It refuses, as the thrown error did, and answers in the package's envelope where the throw left the answer to the host.
- The answer's text names no host, address, adapter or plugin: it says the server cannot judge its reads of an identity provider and that nothing was read or sent. The detail goes to the server log only. Right.
- The branch is reached only when the shipped mount is broken (the observer is mounted with `sso`, and the only other adapter view in the package delegates), so no deployment's answers move and the changeset owes it no line. Right. The PR body names the 503 in its read-first list and its test list.
- The callback door answers the same JSON 503 to a browser, where its ordinary refusals redirect to the error page. Right for a server that cannot serve the door at all; noted, not a finding.
- The docblock of `sso-discovery-egress.ts` now carries the upgrade note for the vendor dependency (model and member names the observer keys on). Right.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: both packages `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 marker, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset and the PR body. The delta publishes nothing new: a private method's refusal changed shape on a branch the shipped configuration does not reach.

- SQL push-down: the delta adds no read, no id materialisation, no in-app join.
- Gates on this head at this read: every check-run is completed; 62 concluded success, 12 skipped, none failed (`Check Changeset` ran twice, both success).
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R6 — graded in the seat's private notes; none blocks this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

S3: closed.
